sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the impugned FIR No. 0116 dated 23.01.2026 registered at P.S. Civil Lines, Bilaspur, alleging offence under Section 420 IPC in relation to a loan transaction of Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited, is a gross misuse of the criminal process.

entities.text: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is contended that the borrower, Late Mohd. Ayyub Khan, along with co-applicant, voluntarily applied for and obtained a secured commercial loan after executing all requisite documents, declarations and insurance proposals.
The loan was disbursed strictly in accordance with company policy, after lawful deductions towards processing fees and insurance premium, which were duly reflected in the signed loan documents.

The allegation that life insurance was promised but medical insurance was issued is factually incorrect and, at best, gives rise to a civil or consumer dispute, particularly in view of the proceedings initiated under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act following default after the borrower's demise.

It is further submitted that the petitioners were merely salaried employees/authorized agents acting in discharge of their official duties without any personal gain or dishonest intention, and have since resigned from service.
The essential ingredients of cheating, namely dishonest inducement at inception and mens rea, are wholly absent.

Placing reliance on the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Haryana and Others v. Bhajan Lal and Others, (1992) Supp. 1 SCC 335, it is urged that even if the allegations in the FIR are taken at face value, no cognizable offence is made out and the continuation of investigation amounts to abuse of process of law, warranting interference under Section 582 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to secure the ends of justice.

entities.text: State of Haryana and Others v. Bhajan Lal and Others, (1992) Supp. 1 SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, issue notice to the respondents by ordinary post as well as speed post.

Learned State counsel appears and accepts notice on behalf of respondents No.1 to 3, therefore,
issuance of notice to them, are dispensed with.
Process Fee be paid within a week for respondent No.4 only.
Notice be made returnable in four weeks.

Two weeks' time is granted to the learned State counsel as well as respondent No.4 to file its reply-affidavit and thereafter, one week's time is granted to the learned counsel for the petitioners to file rejoinder-affidavit.

Till the next date of listing or till submission of Police Report under Section 173(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(now under Section 193(3) of the BNSS), if any, before the competent Court, whichever is earlier, the arrest of the petitioners in pursuance of impugned F.I.R. No. 0116 of 2026 dated 23.01.2026 registered at Police Station Civil Lines, District Bilaspur (C.G.), shall remain stayed, of course subject to the restraint that the petitioners shall fully cooperate with the investigation and shall appear as and when called upon to assist in the investigation.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) (Ramesh Sinha)
